product_or_line: Moosehead Canadian Lager, Moosehead Light, Cracked Canoe and Radler
common_use: Everyday mainstream lager that replaces U.S.-brewed macro beers such as Budweiser, Coors Light or Miller.
made_in_canada_claim: Moosehead's own site headlines the brand as '100% CANADIAN SINCE 1867' and its FAQ confirms the brewery is in Saint John, New Brunswick, describing itself as Canada's oldest independent brewery.
manufacturing_location: Saint John, New Brunswick (89 Main Street West brewery and taproom)
ownership_note: Family owned and operated by the Oland family for six generations; Canada's oldest independent brewery
evidence_quote: 100% CANADIAN SINCE 1867.

product_or_line: Traditional Ale, Grasshopper wheat ale, Honey Brown Lager and Rock Creek ciders
common_use: Craft ales and lagers that replace imported U.S. craft beer brands.
made_in_canada_claim: Big Rock's own management discussion and analysis states its primary brewing, packaging and warehousing facility is in Calgary, Alberta, and calls the company one of Canada's largest independently owned craft brewers.
manufacturing_location: Calgary, Alberta (primary brewery since 1996; additional facilities in Vancouver, BC and Etobicoke/Toronto, ON)
ownership_note: Canadian-headquartered independently owned craft brewer (TSX-listed at time of filing)
evidence_quote: Today, Big Rock's primary brewing, packaging and warehousing facility is located in Calgary, Alberta and has been in operation since 1996.

product_or_line: Muskoka Cream Ale, Detour Session IPA, Mad Tom IPA and Craft Lager
common_use: Craft ales and IPAs that replace U.S. craft imports in the fridge.
made_in_canada_claim: Muskoka Brewery's own story page says the Muskoka region 'is at the heart of what we brew,' that the brewery operates from its Muskoka Beach Rd. location, and confirms it has been independently owned since 1996.
manufacturing_location: Bracebridge, Ontario (1964 Muskoka Beach Road)
ownership_note: Independently owned since 1996; owned and operated by Todd Lewin and Bob MacDonald
evidence_quote: Yes, Muskoka Brewery has been independently owned since 1996 and plans to stay that way!

product_or_line: Belgian-style ales including Blanche de Chambly, La Fin du Monde and Maudite
common_use: Strong Belgian-style bottled ales replacing imported U.S. or Belgian specialty beer.
made_in_canada_claim: Unibroue's About page states its 'ultra-modern site in Chambly' produces its beers and that it has brewed there since 1992, making it the most-awarded brewery in Canada.
manufacturing_location: Chambly, Quebec
ownership_note: Brewed in Quebec but owned by Sleeman Breweries, a subsidiary of Japan's Sapporo
origin_caveat: Foreign parent ownership (Sapporo/Sleeman); beer itself is brewed in Chambly, Quebec.
evidence_quote: Our ultra-modern site in Chambly produces beers with unique flavour profiles through ancestral wisdom inspired by Belgian traditions.

product_or_line: Irish Red Ale, Tall Ship Amber Ale and rotating small-batch craft beer
common_use: Maritime craft beer replacing U.S. craft ales and lagers.
made_in_canada_claim: Garrison's brewery page says its beer is 'fermented in Nova Scotia', that the team is determined to stay '100% SEAPORT BREWED' in Halifax, and that base malt is Maritime-grown.
manufacturing_location: Halifax, Nova Scotia (1149 Marginal Road, Seaport)
ownership_note: Independent Halifax craft brewery founded 1997
origin_caveat: Base malt is Maritime-grown but specialty hops are 'sourced from all over the world' per the brewery.
evidence_quote: From our Maritime-grown base malt to premium, specialty hops sourced from all over the world, we're committed to using only the best.

product_or_line: Blue Buck Ale, Electric Unicorn white IPA and in-house malted beers
common_use: West Coast craft beer replacing U.S. Pacific Northwest craft imports.
made_in_canada_claim: Phillips states it is the only craft brewer in Canada that malts its own barley, using barley grown on Vancouver Island and harvested by local farmers, at its Victoria, BC brewery and malt house.
manufacturing_location: Victoria, British Columbia (2010 Government St.)
ownership_note: Privately held, founded 2000 by Matt Phillips
origin_caveat: Some specialty hops and adjuncts may be imported; base barley is Vancouver Island grown.
evidence_quote: Barley grown right here on Vancouver Island is harvested by local farmers.

product_or_line: Ransack the Universe IPA, Life in the Clouds hazy IPA, plus ciders and RTDs
common_use: Art-label craft beer and hard seltzers replacing U.S. craft and RTD brands.
made_in_canada_claim: Collective Arts describes itself on its own site as 'proudly and creatively Canadian, based in Hamilton, Ontario,' and lists its brewery and taproom at 207 Burlington St. East in Hamilton.
manufacturing_location: Hamilton, Ontario (207 Burlington St. East brewery/taproom)
ownership_note: Founded 2013 by Matt Johnston and Bob Russell
evidence_quote: Collective Arts is proudly and creatively Canadian, based in Hamilton, Ontario, and driven by one bold idea: creativity belongs everywhere.

product_or_line: Organic and biodynamic VQA Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Riesling and Cabernet Franc
common_use: Premium Ontario table wines replacing California and Washington bottles.
made_in_canada_claim: Tawse's own fact sheet states the winery site is located in Vineland, Ontario at 3955 Cherry Avenue in the VQA Twenty Mile Bench appellation, with all estate vineyards farmed organically and biodynamically.
manufacturing_location: Vineland, Ontario (3955 Cherry Avenue, VQA Twenty Mile Bench, Niagara Escarpment)
ownership_note: Owned by founder Moray Tawse
evidence_quote: Winery Site: Located in Vineland Ontario at 3955 Cherry Avenue. VQA Twenty Mile Bench

product_or_line: Beamsville Bench Riesling, Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc and Riesling Icewine
common_use: Niagara cool-climate whites and icewine replacing U.S. wines.
made_in_canada_claim: Cave Spring's About page describes the Pennachetti family planting some of Niagara's first Riesling and Chardonnay vines on the Beamsville Bench and lists its winery office in Jordan, Ontario, Canada; wine is grown and made at Cave Spring Vineyard on the Niagara Escarpment.
manufacturing_location: Jordan / Beamsville, Ontario (winery office 1B-3836 Main Street, Jordan; Cave Spring Vineyard, 4043 Cave Spring Road, Beamsville)
ownership_note: Founded and long operated by the Pennachetti family
evidence_quote: Today, more than four decades after John and his sons took a chance and planted some of Niagara's first Riesling and Chardonnay vines on that plot of land, Cave Spring Vineyard serves as a constant reminder of the good things that can happen when we honour our past to forge a new future.

product_or_line: Okanagan VQA reds, whites and the Legacy Collection
common_use: Premium BC wines replacing Napa/Sonoma bottles.
made_in_canada_claim: Mission Hill's own site says it was 'among the first wineries to realise the potential of the valley' in the Okanagan and that it was named Winery of the Year for a record sixth time at the 2025 WineAlign National Wine Awards of Canada, farming 100% of its own grapes in BC.
manufacturing_location: West Kelowna, British Columbia (Okanagan Valley)
ownership_note: Founded and owned by Anthony von Mandl, who built in his native British Columbia
evidence_quote: Recently named Winery of the Year for a record sixth time at the 2025 WineAlign National Wine Awards of Canada, Mission Hill continues to set the standard in Canadian excellence.

product_or_line: BC VQA Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc and Rosé
common_use: Okanagan estate wines replacing U.S. West Coast wines.
made_in_canada_claim: Quails' Gate says on its own story page that it is a fourth-generation Okanagan farming family that farms 160 acres of vineyards and has been a leader in developing Canadian viticulture practices, producing premium BC VQA wines.
manufacturing_location: West Kelowna, British Columbia (3303 Boucherie Road)
ownership_note: Family owned and operated by the Stewart family since 1989
evidence_quote: We farm 160 acres of vineyards and have been leaders in the development of Canadian viticulture practices.

product_or_line: Qwam Qwmt and Winemaker's Series Okanagan VQA wines
common_use: BC wines from North America's first Indigenous-owned winery, replacing imported U.S. wine.
made_in_canada_claim: Nk'Mip Cellars states on its About page that it is the first Indigenous-owned winery in North America and produces its award-winning wines at its Osoyoos, BC winery on Osoyoos Indian Band land.
manufacturing_location: Osoyoos, British Columbia (1400 Rancher Creek Road)
ownership_note: Indigenous-owned: a venture of the Osoyoos Indian Band (in partnership with Arterra Wines Canada)
origin_caveat: Joint venture with Arterra Wines Canada (itself Canadian-based, owned by Ontario Teachers'/private equity).
evidence_quote: As the first Indigenous-owned winery in North America, we are inspired to express our culture in everything we do.

product_or_line: Nova 7, traditional-method sparkling wine and Tidal Bay whites
common_use: Sparkling and aromatic wines replacing U.S. sparkling wine and prosecco-style imports.
made_in_canada_claim: Benjamin Bridge's story page says it produces the highest quality wines from grapes farmed along the Bay of Fundy in Nova Scotia's Gaspereau Valley and calls itself Canada's premier sparkling wine house.
manufacturing_location: Gaspereau Valley, Nova Scotia (near Wolfville, Annapolis Valley region)
ownership_note: Founded by Nova Scotians Gerry McConnell and the late Dara Gordon; Murphy Hospitality Group became an equal equity partner in 2025
evidence_quote: Over two and a half decades, Benjamin Bridge has distinguished itself as Canada's premier sparkling wine house.

product_or_line: Nova Scotia estate wines including Tidal Bay, L'Acadie Blanc and Marechal Foch
common_use: Atlantic Canadian table wines replacing U.S. wine on the dinner table.
made_in_canada_claim: Domaine de Grand Pré states it is family owned and operated and was 'built on love and passion for Nova Scotia and exceptional wine and food', operating Atlantic Canada's oldest farm winery in the Annapolis Valley.
manufacturing_location: Grand Pré, Nova Scotia (11611 Highway 1, Annapolis Valley)
ownership_note: Family owned and operated by the Stutz family
evidence_quote: Family owned and operated, Domaine de Grand Pré winery was built on love and passion for Nova Scotia and exceptional wine and food.

product_or_line: Quebec white, red, rosé, ice wine and fortified wines
common_use: Quebec-grown table and dessert wines replacing U.S. wines.
made_in_canada_claim: L'Orpailleur's history page states its mission is to offer 'authentically Quebec' wines of superior quality, grown at the Dunham property purchased in the early 1980s that became the Vignoble de l'Orpailleur.
manufacturing_location: Dunham, Quebec (1086 rue Bruce, Brome-Missisquoi, Eastern Townships)
ownership_note: Co-owned by its founding vignerons, including Charles-Henri de Coussergues, and now second-generation family members
evidence_quote: Notre mission est d'offrir des vins authentiquement québécois, de qualité supérieure, qui répondent aux plus hauts standards en vitiviniculture.

product_or_line: J.P. Wiser's Deluxe, Special Blend and aged Canadian whiskies
common_use: Everyday Canadian rye whisky replacing American bourbon and Tennessee whiskey.
made_in_canada_claim: J.P. Wiser's official site states the Hiram Walker & Sons Distillery in Windsor, Ontario is 'the home of Canadian whisky' and that this historic facility produces some of the best whiskies in Canada, with the brand marked 'Wisely crafted in Windsor, Ontario'.
manufacturing_location: Windsor, Ontario (Hiram Walker & Sons Distillery, 2072 Riverside Drive East)
ownership_note: Distilled in Canada; brand marketed by Corby Spirit and Wine, majority-owned by France's Pernod Ricard
origin_caveat: Foreign parent ownership (Pernod Ricard/Corby); whisky is distilled, aged and bottled in Windsor, Ontario.
evidence_quote: The Hiram Walker & Sons Distillery in Windsor, Ontario is the home of Canadian whisky and one of North America's largest distilleries.

product_or_line: Alberta Premium 100% rye whisky, Alberta Springs, Alberta Pure vodka
common_use: 100% rye Canadian whisky replacing U.S. rye and bourbon.
made_in_canada_claim: Alberta Distillers' brand page states Alberta Premium 'is a proudly Canadian whisky, crafted in Calgary since 1958 using 100% rye grain and pure Rocky Mountain water'.
manufacturing_location: Calgary, Alberta (Alberta Distillers Ltd.)
ownership_note: Distilled in Calgary; parent company is Suntory Global Spirits (Japan)
origin_caveat: Foreign parent ownership (Suntory); grain is locally sourced Alberta rye.
evidence_quote: Alberta Premium is a proudly Canadian whisky, crafted in Calgary since 1958 using 100% rye grain and pure Rocky Mountain water.

product_or_line: Shelter Point Classic Single Malt, Artisanal Single Malt and Cask Strength whiskies
common_use: Farm-to-flask single malt whisky replacing imported American whiskey.
made_in_canada_claim: Shelter Point's About page says the distillery, built in 2011, is located on the coast in northern Vancouver Island and distils and matures whisky on site, with the team working to elevate Vancouver Island as a premium single malt region; the company describes its whisky as a '100% Canadian take on single malt'.
manufacturing_location: Campbell River, British Columbia (4692 Regent Road, Oyster River / Vancouver Island)
ownership_note: Farm-based distillery on a coastal Vancouver Island estate growing its own barley
origin_caveat: Some casks (ex-bourbon, sherry) and equipment are imported.
evidence_quote: Located on the coast in northern Vancouver Island, the distillery has become a destination not only just for fine whisky but also for the spectacular setting and onsite experience.

product_or_line: Glen Breton Rare Canadian single malt whisky, 10-year and ice wine barrel expressions
common_use: Canadian single malt whisky replacing imported American and Scotch whisky.
made_in_canada_claim: Glenora's own distillery page states it is located in Nova Scotia on Cape Breton Island and is recognized as the first single malt whisky distillery in North America, producing Glen Breton from barley, yeast and water in copper pot stills.
manufacturing_location: Glenville, Cape Breton Island, Nova Scotia
ownership_note: Independently owned by Glenora Distillers International Ltd.
origin_caveat: Barley may be imported/Scottish-style malt; distillation and maturation are on site in Nova Scotia.
evidence_quote: Glenora is located in Nova Scotia, a province whose name literally translates to 'New Scotland.'

product_or_line: Stalk & Barrel Single Malt, Rye and Cask Strength Canadian whiskies, plus vodka
common_use: Small-batch Ontario grain whisky replacing U.S. craft bourbon and rye.
made_in_canada_claim: Still Waters states its Stalk & Barrel Rye is 'made from locally sourced 100% Ontario rye grain', mashed, fermented and distilled by hand in a copper pot still and matured on site at its Concord, Ontario craft distillery.
manufacturing_location: Concord (Vaughan), Ontario (150 Bradwick Dr Unit #26)
ownership_note: Independent micro-distillery founded 2009 by Barry Stein and Barry Bernstein; Ontario's first micro-distillery
evidence_quote: Made from locally sourced 100% Ontario rye grain.

product_or_line: Two Brewers Yukon Single Malt Whisky, released in numbered small batches
common_use: Northern Canadian single malt whisky replacing imported American whiskey.
made_in_canada_claim: Two Brewers' own About page says founders Bob Baxter and Al Hansen began brewing in Whitehorse in 1997 and later started making whisky there, and that the company services the North 'keeping jobs and money in the territory'.
manufacturing_location: Whitehorse, Yukon (102 Copper Road, shared with Yukon Brewing)
ownership_note: Independently owned by its two founders
origin_caveat: Malted grains are sourced from southern suppliers; distillation, maturation and bottling occur in Whitehorse.
evidence_quote: We may have started as just two brewers, but Two Brewers has grown into so much more, servicing the North with quality spirits, keeping jobs and money in the territory, and supporting our local community.

product_or_line: Iceberg Vodka made with Canadian corn and harvested iceberg water
common_use: Mixing and cocktail vodka replacing U.S. brands such as Tito's or Smirnoff's U.S.-made bottlings.
made_in_canada_claim: Iceberg's site states 'Iceberg Vodka is not just made in Canada; it's made of Canada', that it uses premium Canadian corn grown on local farms, and that every step from foraging to distillation, bottling and packaging happens in Canada.
manufacturing_location: Newfoundland and Labrador (icebergs harvested off the NL coast; company headquartered in St. John's, NL)
ownership_note: Canadian company founded in Newfoundland in 1995
origin_caveat: Corn is Canadian (reported as Ontario corn by trade databases); official site does not name the exact distillation plant.
evidence_quote: Iceberg Vodka is not just made in Canada; it's made of Canada.

product_or_line: Crystal Head Original, Onyx and Aurora vodkas in the skull bottle
common_use: Premium cocktail and gift vodka replacing U.S. premium vodka brands.
made_in_canada_claim: Crystal Head's FAQ states the vodka 'is produced in St. John's, Newfoundland' and that the spirit is quadruple distilled and blended with pristine water from Newfoundland, Canada; the Original expression is distilled from locally sourced Canadian corn.
manufacturing_location: St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador (Rock Spirits facility)
ownership_note: Produced by Globefill Inc., co-founded by Canadian actor Dan Aykroyd; bottled at the Newfoundland and Labrador Liquor Corporation's Rock Spirits plant
origin_caveat: Original and Onyx use Canadian corn; the Aurora expression uses English-grown wheat blended with Newfoundland water.
evidence_quote: Crystal Head Vodka is produced in St. John's, Newfoundland, on an island off the Canadian coast, at one of the last government-owned distilleries in the world.

product_or_line: Vodka Terroir, Gin Sauvage and Quebec fruit vodkas, all grain-to-bottle
common_use: Grain-to-bottle vodka and gin replacing U.S. craft spirits.
made_in_canada_claim: Cirka's About page says it is the first grain-to-bottle distillery in Quebec, producing spirits from local grain at its distillery along the Lachine Canal in Montreal since 2016, sourcing from local farmers and foragers.
manufacturing_location: Montreal, Quebec (Lachine Canal, Saint-Henri district)
ownership_note: Independent micro-distillery founded by Paul Cirka
evidence_quote: Inspired by microdistilleries across North America and the high quality of homegrown products across the province, we became the first Québec microdistillery to produce spirits from grain-to-bottle, a new concept in the region.

product_or_line: Seaside Gin, Beacon Gin, vodka and akvavit
common_use: Craft gin for cocktails, replacing U.S. craft gins.
made_in_canada_claim: Sheringham's About page describes founders Jason and Alayne MacIsaac building their first distillery in Shirley, B.C. on southern Vancouver Island, and the distillery says its spirits are distilled with locally foraged botanicals including Vancouver Island kelp.
manufacturing_location: Langford, British Columbia (relocated from Shirley/Sooke, Vancouver Island)
ownership_note: Family business founded and run by Jason and Alayne MacIsaac
origin_caveat: Some botanicals (e.g. citrus, cardamom, coriander) are imported; distillation is on Vancouver Island.
evidence_quote: Starting from scratch, Jason and Alayne MacIsaac gradually built their first distillery in their garage at home in Shirley, B.C., a humble Southern Vancouver Island town whose original name was Sheringham.

product_or_line: Empress 1908 Indigo Gin, Victoria Gin, oaken gin and liqueurs
common_use: Premium colour-changing gin for cocktails, replacing U.S. premium gin.
made_in_canada_claim: Victoria Distillers states its 'unique waterfront location in Sidney, British Columbia, houses the copper pot stills that produce our range of spirits' and that it has produced some of Canada's finest handmade spirits for more than ten years.
manufacturing_location: Sidney, British Columbia (waterfront distillery, Vancouver Island)
ownership_note: One of Canada's oldest small-batch spirits companies
origin_caveat: Distillery states it uses 'the highest quality ingredients from around the world', including butterfly pea blossom sourced from Thailand.
evidence_quote: Our unique waterfront location in Sidney, British Columbia, houses the copper pot stills that produce our range of spirits - most notably, our award-winning gins.

product_or_line: BC single malt and rye whiskies, gins, vodkas, fruit liqueurs and brandies
common_use: Farm-to-flask BC spirits replacing U.S. whiskey, gin and fruit liqueurs.
made_in_canada_claim: Okanagan Spirits states it is Western Canada's original craft distillery, making Canadian spirits from 100% B.C. grain and fruit in Vernon and Kelowna, BC since 2004, with only on-site fermentation and distillation.
manufacturing_location: Vernon and Kelowna, British Columbia
ownership_note: Small, family-run BC craft distillery
evidence_quote: Okanagan Spirits is Western Canada's original craft distillery making authentic, internationally awarded Canadian spirits from 100% B.C. grain and fruit in Vernon & Kelowna, BC since 2004.

product_or_line: Traditional-method sparkling ciders, rosé cider and ice cider from Geneva red-fleshed apples
common_use: Sparkling and ice ciders replacing imported U.S. hard cider.
made_in_canada_claim: The cidery's own page states Michel Jodoin is the fourth generation of apple growers in the Jodoin family established in Rougemont, Quebec in 1901, and that he received one of Quebec's first permits to produce and sell artisanal cider, which he still makes there.
manufacturing_location: Rougemont, Quebec (Montérégie)
ownership_note: Family-run cidery, fourth-generation apple growers
evidence_quote: Michel represents the fourth generation of apple growers in the Jodoin family, established in Rougemont in 1901!

product_or_line: Traditionally fermented organic ciders including Wild English and Rumrunner
common_use: Dry farmhouse cider replacing U.S. hard ciders.
made_in_canada_claim: Sea Cider's About page says it is a farm-based cidery located on the Saanich Peninsula on the south end of Vancouver Island, with a ten-acre farm of over 1,300 heirloom apple trees, crafting traditionally fermented ciders from organically grown apples.
manufacturing_location: Saanichton (Central Saanich), British Columbia (2487 Mt. St. Michael Road)
ownership_note: Family-owned orchard and ciderhouse founded in 2007 by owner Kristen Needham
evidence_quote: Sea Cider is a farm-based cidery located on the Saanich Peninsula just minutes from Victoria, on the south end of Vancouver Island.

product_or_line: Waupoos Premium cider, County Apple, ice cider and fruit ciders
common_use: Orchard-based Ontario cider replacing U.S. hard cider brands.
made_in_canada_claim: County Cider states on its own site that its cider is 'freshly made right here in Prince Edward County' from orchard-ripened apples at its Waupoos, Ontario estate.
manufacturing_location: Waupoos (Prince Edward County), Ontario (657 Bongards Crossroad)
ownership_note: Family-operated estate cidery and winery operating since the 1990s
evidence_quote: At County Cider, we are known for our wonderful tasting cider that is freshly made right here in Prince Edward County.
